title: Tensile minimal surfaces and thread boundary problems
summary: Minimal surfaces bounded by cables or threads arise naturally in tensile architecture: a membrane under uniform tension takes the shape of a minimal surface, and its flexible, inextensible boundary lies along an asymptotic line of constant geodesic curvature. Such configurations have been studied experimentally since the 1960s at the Institute for Lightweight Structures in Stuttgart and more recently realized in gridshells built along networks of asymptotic and geodesic curves.
